To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
p53 is downregulated in human schwannoma, and that p53 is regulated in schwannoma cells by merlin via FAK and AKT.
p53 and MDM2 deregulation in merlindisrupted schwannoma cells is responsible for the development and maintenance of these tumours.
p53 is downregulated and MDM2 is upregulated in schwannoma cells leading to increased cell survival and proliferation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the tumour-suppressors merlin and p53 in the development of schwanno-mas, meningiomas, ependymomas and mesotheliomas and the development of novel therapeutic approaches for these tumours.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in tumour development and progression, with the aim to identify novel therapeutic targets for cancer treatment.
the role of p63 in the development of merlindeficient tumours.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the p53/ MDM2 complex is deregulated in human primary schwannomas and this is a novel finding that could be used as a potential therapeutic target.
the loss of merlin in schwannoma cells results in increased cell proliferation and cell survival.
the p53/mouse-double minute 2 homologue (MDM2) pathway is dysregulated in merlin-defective schwannoma cells, and that this dysregulation is associated with tumorigenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the merlin-deficiency in schwannoma cells leads to an increase of FAK activity and localisation into the nucleus.
we have shown that merlin-deficient schwannoma cells have increased proliferation, survival and p53 deregulation due to the increased activity of the FAK and PI3K/Akt pathways.
merlin-deficient schwannoma cells have a deregulated p53/MD2 complex leading to increased proliferation and survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
p53 is downregulated in merlin-defective tumours and that this is mediated by MDM2 and that this is important in tumour development and progression.
merlin loss deregulates the p53/ MDM2 pathway leading to the development of merlindisrupted tumours and that p53 is a potential therapeutic target for these tumours.
the p53/merlin/MDM2 axis is deregulated in human primary schwannomas.
